<!-- The description is the plan (docs/workflow.md). Open the pull request as a draft and wait for approval before implementing. The pull-request check requires every section below. -->

## Issue

<!-- "Closes #12" or "Relates to #12". "None" only with a reason. -->

## Goal

<!-- What is different after the merge, in one to three sentences. -->

## Acceptance criteria

<!-- A checklist. Each item is an observable result plus the proof that shows it (test, recording or screenshots, CI job). Check an item off ("- [x]") as soon as it is done and proven; open items are allowed only while the pull request is a draft. Work that can only happen after the merge (for example publishing a release) is not a criterion: put it in Approach and give it its own issue. -->

## Approach

<!-- Ordered steps. Name the files, modules or packages each step touches. -->

## Affected surfaces

<!-- Packages, runtimes (web, desktop, hosted mobile, Capacitor mobile), user-visible states, persisted or external contracts. Explain why an apparently applicable runtime is unaffected. -->

## Repository guidance

<!-- The AGENTS.md rules, project skills, skill references and nearest README/DOCUMENTATION.md files used, why each applies and how the change complies. A table works well: | Guidance | Why it applies | How the change complies | -->

## Verification

<!-- How the change is proven: exact commands and results, tests by name or file, and what was not verified. User-visible changes need a recording (preferred) or screenshots of the real program, before and after when behavior changes, for the affected desktop/mobile, narrow/wide and theme states (CONTRIBUTING.md). Look at every screenshot and the whole recording before attaching, and say so. For each proof: how a developer reproduces it (commands from a fresh checkout, URL, what to look at). No visible change: explain why the diff cannot affect rendered behavior. -->

## Decisions

<!-- New or superseded records in docs/adr/, with number and title. Or "None". -->

## Findings

<!-- Added to CONTEXT.md: what this pull request learned outside the code (GitHub, another repository, a real system, a measurement), by entry title. Removed from CONTEXT.md: the entries it settles, and where they went. Or "None". -->

## Out of scope

<!-- What this pull request deliberately does not do. -->

## Risks and open questions

<!-- Failure, rollback, cleanup, compatibility, security, performance, data-loss and cross-runtime concerns the reviewer should look at closely. "None identified" only with a concrete reason. -->
